world.title: Russian crews tow drone-hit cargo ship out of Finnish waters
world.summary: A Russian rescue vessel towed the drone-damaged cargo ship Sparta II out of Finnish waters after it caught fire following a suspected Ukrainian strike in the Gulf of Finland on Nov. 21. Finnish President Alexander Stubb said the ship had left Finnish waters. Kyiv has not claimed responsibility for the attack. All 16 cr
world.content: A Russian rescue vessel towed the drone-damaged cargo ship Sparta II out of Finnish waters after it caught fire following a suspected Ukrainian strike in the Gulf of Finland on Nov. 21. Finnish President Alexander Stubb said the ship had left Finnish waters. Kyiv has not claimed responsibility for the attack. All 16 crew members had been evacuated to another Russian vessel, and one was slightly injured. Finnish, Russian and Estonian vessels fought the fire for two days. Thermal cameras still detected heat in some containers, but Finnish authorities said the ship was stable enough to tow and reported no leaks of fuel or hazardous substances. The Finnish Coast Guard said it would hand responsibility for the rescue to Russia once the ship left Finnish waters. Finnish authorities said the situation was under control, with no environmental damage, while the investigation into a suspected violation of Finnish airspace by an aircraft continued.

world.title: Trump hosts dinner for $TRUMP holders as coin sinks below $1
world.summary: President Donald Trump hosted a private dinner for major holders of his $TRUMP meme coin Sunday, Nov. 22, at his golf club in Sterling, Virginia. Trump told attendees he backed cryptocurrency to strengthen U.S. economic competitiveness. The coin, which once reached about $75, was trading below $1. The 130 wallets on th
world.content: President Donald Trump hosted a private dinner for major holders of his $TRUMP meme coin Sunday, Nov. 22, at his golf club in Sterling, Virginia. Trump told attendees he backed cryptocurrency to strengthen U.S. economic competitiveness. The coin, which once reached about $75, was trading below $1. The 130 wallets on the dinner leaderboard held a combined $8.6 million, compared with $148 million listed for the May 2025 dinner. Trump’s June financial disclosure showed the family had earned at least $635 million from the coin, while outside investors in five Trump family crypto-linked projects had lost more than $5 billion, according to a Reuters analysis. Democrats, who won majorities in both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections, have pledged inquiries into potential conflicts of interest when the new members take office next year. The White House has said the dinner was a private event, not a government function.
world.image_alt: Trump hosts dinner for $TRUMP holders as coin sinks below $1

world.title: U.S. tracked Alice Huang’s China intelligence contacts during Nvidia affair
world.summary: U.S. intelligence tracked Alice Huang’s contacts with an officer of China’s Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 through fall 2026, a period that overlapped with her relationship with former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, according to people familiar with intelligence reports. U.S. agencies also gathered e
world.content: U.S. intelligence tracked Alice Huang’s contacts with an officer of China’s Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 through fall 2026, a period that overlapped with her relationship with former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, according to people familiar with intelligence reports. U.S. agencies also gathered evidence that her business partner Kang Wei worked with the same agency. The Justice Department has not determined whether Alice Huang spied for China and is investigating her and her company. Alice Huang previously led Singapore-based Megaspeed International, a major Nvidia customer under U.S. investigation since 2024 over suspected shipments of advanced chips to China. Intelligence reports cited by The New York Times include shipping records linking Alice Huang and Kang to a network of companies. Some chips bought by Megaspeed went to Southeast Asian data centers serving Chinese technology firms, while others are suspected of having been smuggled into China. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the government wants to establish who oversaw Nvidia’s compliance with export controls. The Securities and Exchange Commission is also examining Nvidia’s accounting, though the inquiry’s focus and any connection to the chip allegations remain unclear. President Donald Trump has played down the espionage concerns and urged Nvidia to bring Jensen Huang back, but the company’s board has ruled out his return. Huang is scheduled to face lawmakers on Dec. 1.
world.image_alt: U.S. tracked Alice Huang’s China intelligence contacts during Nvidia affair

world.title: Drone strikes damage homes and U.N. building in Sudan
world.summary: Drone strikes damaged homes and a United Nations facility in Khartoum early Sunday. Local reports cited by Australia’s ABC said at least four civilians were killed and nine injured. Witnesses reported explosions near the airport and elsewhere in the city from about 2 a.m. to 4:30 a.m. One house was destroyed, and a str
world.content: Drone strikes damaged homes and a United Nations facility in Khartoum early Sunday. Local reports cited by Australia’s ABC said at least four civilians were killed and nine injured. Witnesses reported explosions near the airport and elsewhere in the city from about 2 a.m. to 4:30 a.m. One house was destroyed, and a strike was also reported in Jebel Aulia, south of the capital. A Sudanese army source alleged that the drones were launched from Ethiopia’s Bahir Dar airport and accused Addis Ababa of enabling the attacks. Ethiopia denies the accusations. ABC reported that the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the paramilitary group fighting Sudan’s army, were blamed for the strikes, but the accounts did not independently establish responsibility. The United Nations said its premises were damaged while staff were inside, and its humanitarian office condemned the danger to civilians and aid workers. The war between the army and RSF began in April 2023; aid workers estimate it has killed more than 200,000 people. The U.N. Human Rights Office reported that drone attacks killed more than 1,630 civilians in Sudan between January and October 2026.
world.image_alt: Drone strikes damage homes and U.N. building in Sudan

world.title: US intelligence chief backs Trump
world.summary: U.S. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton on Sunday defended President Donald Trump’s description of Russian President Vladimir Putin as his friend, saying the wording was appropriate given Trump’s Nov. 19 meeting with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. Clayton also said Putin was not America’
world.content: U.S. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton on Sunday defended President Donald Trump’s description of Russian President Vladimir Putin as his friend, saying the wording was appropriate given Trump’s Nov. 19 meeting with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. Clayton also said Putin was not America’s friend in Ukraine, where Russia is waging war. Clayton described the gathering of the three nuclear powers as historic and said their leaders agreed to reduce nuclear risks and communicate with one another; critics noted that the meeting produced no firm commitments. Trump defended calling Putin a friend on Thursday, saying it was better to have nuclear-armed leaders as friends than enemies. On Friday, he declined to say whether Putin was a friend of the United States. The comments drew criticism from U.S. lawmakers and Ukraine’s European allies. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described Putin as an enemy and a killer, while Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Putin would never be Poland’s friend. Russia controls about a fifth of Ukraine, and Putin has maintained his demand that Ukraine cede the entire Donbas region as part of a peace deal.

world.title: Russian strikes kill 15 in Kyiv region as rescuers search rubble
world.summary: Russian strikes across Ukraine’s Kyiv region killed at least 15 people on Sunday, Ukrainian officials said, while rescue workers searched the rubble of a partly collapsed apartment block in Dymer on Monday. Eleven people died in the five-story building. A strike on a supermarket in Vyshneve killed three and wounded 15,
world.content: Russian strikes across Ukraine’s Kyiv region killed at least 15 people on Sunday, Ukrainian officials said, while rescue workers searched the rubble of a partly collapsed apartment block in Dymer on Monday. Eleven people died in the five-story building. A strike on a supermarket in Vyshneve killed three and wounded 15, including three children, and another person died when a strike hit a home in Bila Tserkva. The attacks also hit a power substation in Dnipropetrovsk region as temperatures approached freezing. Ukrainian officials say Russia has stepped up strikes on energy infrastructure as the country faces another winter nearly five years into Russia’s invasion. President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia launched 2,700 drones and 1,460 aerial bombs over the previous week. More than 130 rescuers took part in the Dymer operation, which renewed air-raid alerts complicated, according to Zelensky. A day of mourning was declared in the Kyiv region for Nov. 23, and NATO was due to discuss the war and its effects in Europe at a meeting Monday.
world.image_alt: Russian strikes kill 15 in Kyiv region as rescuers search rubble

world.title: Netanyahu’s and Eisenkot’s parties end talks without coalition deal
world.summary: Israel’s caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party and Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party ended four hours of coalition talks in Herzliya on Sunday without an agreement, as Eisenkot tries to form a government after an inconclusive October election. The parties said they would meet again but gave no date; Eise
world.content: Israel’s caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party and Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party ended four hours of coalition talks in Herzliya on Sunday without an agreement, as Eisenkot tries to form a government after an inconclusive October election. The parties said they would meet again but gave no date; Eisenkot’s mandate expires Dec. 6, with a possible 14-day extension. Negotiators remained divided over who would lead a unity government, whether far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir could join, judicial legislation and military-service rules for ultra-Orthodox Jewish men. They also discussed a commission of inquiry into the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack but disagreed over how to appoint its members. Eisenkot’s bloc is also exploring support from ultra-Orthodox parties, while Democrats leader Yair Golan advocates a minority government backed by Arab lawmakers. The Times of Israel reported progress in parallel talks with United Torah Judaism on conscription, though the sides had yet to exchange proposals. Eisenkot is expected to present a revised framework this week.
world.image_alt: Netanyahu’s and Eisenkot’s parties end talks without coalition deal

world.title: Indonesia confirms 24 dead as rescuers search candy factory ruins
world.summary: Indonesian authorities on Monday confirmed 24 deaths and said about 30 workers remained missing after a weekend fire at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia candy factory in Cikande, west of Jakarta. Rescuers continued searching the burned site, where unstable structures and lingering hot spots endangered crews; 29 people were co
world.content: Indonesian authorities on Monday confirmed 24 deaths and said about 30 workers remained missing after a weekend fire at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia candy factory in Cikande, west of Jakarta. Rescuers continued searching the burned site, where unstable structures and lingering hot spots endangered crews; 29 people were confirmed safe, including five who were hospitalized. The factory’s chief executive, Steven Erwin Wijaya, said about 300 people were at the complex for Saturday’s shift. Presidential labor adviser Said Iqbal said investigators were assessing whether safety protocols had been followed. He said preliminary information pointed to a possible air-conditioner short circuit, but authorities have not established the cause. The fire left many remains too badly damaged for visual identification, so police are collecting DNA samples from relatives and personal belongings. Identification could take two to three weeks. Search operations and the safety inquiry are continuing.
world.image_alt: Indonesia confirms 24 dead as rescuers search candy factory ruins

business.title: Tata Steel to acquire APL Apollo stake, sell units in ₹28,000 crore deal
business.summary: Tata Steel will acquire a 26.6% promoter stake in APL Apollo Tubes for about ₹15,510 crore and make an offer for a further 26%. It will also sell its steel-tubes business and Tata Steel Colors to APL Apollo for a combined ₹28,000 crore. If the open offer is fully subscribed, Tata Steel would hold a majority stake in th
business.content: Tata Steel will acquire a 26.6% promoter stake in APL Apollo Tubes for about ₹15,510 crore and make an offer for a further 26%. It will also sell its steel-tubes business and Tata Steel Colors to APL Apollo for a combined ₹28,000 crore. If the open offer is fully subscribed, Tata Steel would hold a majority stake in the listed steel-products maker. The transactions would combine Tata Steel’s tubes and colour-coated operations with APL Apollo’s distribution and manufacturing operations, expanding APL Apollo’s downstream products business and Tata Steel’s shareholding in it. Tata Steel expects the stake transactions to close in fiscal 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. The business transfers also require approvals and have a stated long-stop date of March 31, 2028.
business.image_alt: Tata Steel to acquire APL Apollo stake, sell units in ₹28,000 crore deal

business.title: Trump
business.summary: President Donald Trump hosted a third dinner for $TRUMP cryptocurrency holders on Nov. 22 at his golf club in Sterling, Virginia. The public leaderboard listed 130 wallets holding a combined $8.6 million in tokens, while organizers said 185 wallets qualified. The first dinner’s leaderboard listed $148 million in holdin
business.content: President Donald Trump hosted a third dinner for $TRUMP cryptocurrency holders on Nov. 22 at his golf club in Sterling, Virginia. The public leaderboard listed 130 wallets holding a combined $8.6 million in tokens, while organizers said 185 wallets qualified. The first dinner’s leaderboard listed $148 million in holdings. A blockchain analysis prepared for Reuters by consumer advocacy group Public Citizen found that more than half of the listed wallets were linked to crypto exchanges that bar U.S. users, indicating possible foreign ownership. Morten Christensen, founder of cryptocurrency platform Airdrop Alert, said he used a hedge to qualify for a VIP reception but was denied a wristband and removed after speaking with journalists.

business.title: U.S. holiday spending set to top $1 trillion as debt rises
business.summary: U.S. holiday retail sales are forecast to exceed $1 trillion for the first time this year, while Cyber Monday spending is expected to top $15 billion as shoppers face higher living costs. The National Retail Federation projects sales growth of 4.2%, but Visa estimates inflation-adjusted holiday spending will rise only
business.content: U.S. holiday retail sales are forecast to exceed $1 trillion for the first time this year, while Cyber Monday spending is expected to top $15 billion as shoppers face higher living costs. The National Retail Federation projects sales growth of 4.2%, but Visa estimates inflation-adjusted holiday spending will rise only 1.1% as holiday-related prices increase about 3.4%. Household debt rose nearly 2% in the latest quarter, including a $22 billion increase in credit-card balances. Economists surveyed by Bloomberg estimated that inflation-adjusted personal spending grew 0.1% in October; government figures were due Wednesday.
business.image_alt: U.S. holiday spending set to top $1 trillion as debt rises

business.title: Medicare premiums trim 2027 Social Security increase for retirees
business.summary: Medicare Part B premiums will rise by $6.50 a month in 2027, reducing the take-home value of the 3.6% Social Security cost-of-living increase for beneficiaries whose premiums are deducted from their checks. The average Social Security benefit will increase by about $75 a month, from $2,085 to $2,170; the higher Part B
business.content: Medicare Part B premiums will rise by $6.50 a month in 2027, reducing the take-home value of the 3.6% Social Security cost-of-living increase for beneficiaries whose premiums are deducted from their checks. The average Social Security benefit will increase by about $75 a month, from $2,085 to $2,170; the higher Part B premium will offset roughly one month’s worth of that annual increase. The adjustment begins with January payments. Retirees’ costs will also depend on their drug and health plans. Medicare’s annual open enrollment runs through Dec. 7, and plan choices take effect Jan. 1.
business.image_alt: Medicare premiums trim 2027 Social Security increase for retirees

business.title: Trump renews push for 10% credit card rate cap
business.summary: President Donald Trump said he would work with the incoming Democratic-controlled Congress to cap credit card interest rates at 10%, reviving a proposal to limit what issuers charge borrowers. In a Nov. 21 Fox News interview, Trump said card companies had made too much money and defended the cap against objections that
business.content: President Donald Trump said he would work with the incoming Democratic-controlled Congress to cap credit card interest rates at 10%, reviving a proposal to limit what issuers charge borrowers. In a Nov. 21 Fox News interview, Trump said card companies had made too much money and defended the cap against objections that it would interfere with free enterprise. The measure has gained little traction under Republican control, but Democrats are set to take charge of both chambers in January. The proposed ceiling is well below the roughly 22.2% median credit card rate reported in an August New York Federal Reserve survey. Researchers estimate a 10% cap could save Americans about $100 billion a year in interest, while card issuers could remain profitable by reducing rewards and other benefits.
business.image_alt: Trump renews push for 10% credit card rate cap

business.title: India factory growth offsets slower services expansion in November PMI
business.summary: India’s private-sector activity edged higher in November as stronger factory demand and output offset slower services growth, according to HSBC’s flash purchasing managers’ index (PMI), compiled by S&P Global. The composite index rose to 56.3 from 56.2 in October, while the manufacturing index climbed to 56.0, its high
business.content: India’s private-sector activity edged higher in November as stronger factory demand and output offset slower services growth, according to HSBC’s flash purchasing managers’ index (PMI), compiled by S&P Global. The composite index rose to 56.3 from 56.2 in October, while the manufacturing index climbed to 56.0, its highest in nine months; readings above 50 indicate expansion. Manufacturers added staff at the fastest pace in seven months, while services firms cut jobs for the first time in nearly a year. A Reuters poll pointed to slower economic expansion in the October-December quarter, with the fading effect of earlier tax cuts and higher borrowing costs expected to weigh on spending.
business.image_alt: India factory growth offsets slower services expansion in November PMI

business.title: US intelligence chief warns of outages after Delta failure in Atlanta
business.summary: U.S. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Sunday that technology disruptions could continue as companies and government agencies upgrade aging systems and strengthen cybersecurity. He spoke as a software failure at Delta Air Lines’ Atlanta hub delayed flights days before Thanksgiving, following recent d
business.content: U.S. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Sunday that technology disruptions could continue as companies and government agencies upgrade aging systems and strengthen cybersecurity. He spoke as a software failure at Delta Air Lines’ Atlanta hub delayed flights days before Thanksgiving, following recent disruptions to U.S. air travel, Microsoft email, banks and the National Security Agency’s network. Clayton said officials had found no evidence that the recent outages resulted from a coordinated or state-sponsored attack and attributed them to technical problems during upgrades. Delta said a failure in its weight-and-balance software required staff to use manual procedures while engineers restored the system. The airline said the tool was back online later Sunday, though its schedule remained disrupted.
business.image_alt: US intelligence chief warns of outages after Delta failure in Atlanta

business.title: Dutch court blocks BYD SUV sales in EU over Defender design
business.summary: The District Court of The Hague has temporarily barred Chinese automaker BYD from selling its seven-seat Ti7 SUV in the European Union, ruling that its design infringes Jaguar Land Rover’s (JLR) EU design rights for the Defender. The order also halts production of the SUV at BYD’s new plant in Hungary while the case pr
business.content: The District Court of The Hague has temporarily barred Chinese automaker BYD from selling its seven-seat Ti7 SUV in the European Union, ruling that its design infringes Jaguar Land Rover’s (JLR) EU design rights for the Defender. The order also halts production of the SUV at BYD’s new plant in Hungary while the case proceeds. The injunction takes effect one week after Friday’s ruling. The court said BYD had no concrete plans to launch the Ti7 in the EU. It also said it lacked jurisdiction over BYD’s UK business, where deliveries are scheduled to begin in January 2027. BYD says it will appeal and maintains that the Ti7 was independently designed, while JLR says it takes legal action to protect its intellectual property. A final decision on the infringement claim is expected next year. BYD had planned to bring the model to Europe as it expands overseas to offset pressure on profits in China.
business.image_alt: Dutch court blocks BYD SUV sales in EU over Defender design

science.title: Gemini telescope image shows two galaxies triggering new star formation
science.summary: A Gemini North telescope image shows NGC 7253, a pair of spiral galaxies whose mutual gravity is distorting their arms and triggering star formation. The pair lies about 200 million light-years away in the constellation Pegasus. The interaction does not mean stars are colliding: they are too far apart. Instead, gravity
science.content: A Gemini North telescope image shows NGC 7253, a pair of spiral galaxies whose mutual gravity is distorting their arms and triggering star formation. The pair lies about 200 million light-years away in the constellation Pegasus. The interaction does not mean stars are colliding: they are too far apart. Instead, gravity compresses clouds of gas and dust, which can collapse to form stars. The encounter may eventually merge the galaxies into one.
science.image_alt: Gemini telescope image shows two galaxies triggering new star formation

science.title: Super El Niño threatens food supplies as drought hits tropics
science.summary: A powerful 2026-27 El Niño is intensifying, with drought already damaging crops and fisheries in some regions. The World Food Programme warned the event could push another 49 million people into acute food insecurity by the end of 2027, bringing the total to 274 million. El Niño shifts rainfall unevenly, bringing droug
science.content: A powerful 2026-27 El Niño is intensifying, with drought already damaging crops and fisheries in some regions. The World Food Programme warned the event could push another 49 million people into acute food insecurity by the end of 2027, bringing the total to 274 million. El Niño shifts rainfall unevenly, bringing drought to some tropical regions and wetter conditions to others. Moisture from the event has improved conditions for U.S. winter wheat, which is in its best condition since 2018. Climate scientist Christopher Callahan of Indiana University expects global economic losses to reach trillions of dollars over several years, though the toll will become clearer in coming months.
science.image_alt: Super El Niño threatens food supplies as drought hits tropics

science.title: Webb and gravitational waves reveal clues to black hole origins
science.summary: A James Webb Space Telescope study identified a possible black hole in the young galaxy MARTA 3887, seen as it was about 12 billion years ago. Its estimated mass is 3.3 million suns—about 2.3% of the galaxy’s stellar mass. Separately, researchers analyzing 257 black-hole mergers found a concentration near 10 solar mass
science.content: A James Webb Space Telescope study identified a possible black hole in the young galaxy MARTA 3887, seen as it was about 12 billion years ago. Its estimated mass is 3.3 million suns—about 2.3% of the galaxy’s stellar mass. Separately, researchers analyzing 257 black-hole mergers found a concentration near 10 solar masses and a shortage between 12 and 16, a pattern consistent with some massive stars collapsing without supernova explosions. The Webb team says a supernova or gas outflow could mimic the black-hole signal, and its evidence comes from a single observation. The merger study does not directly confirm failed supernovae; researchers say more work is needed to test that explanation.
science.image_alt: Webb and gravitational waves reveal clues to black hole origins

science.title: Earth sets record heat anomaly as Antarctic ozone hole ranks seventh largest
science.summary: Preliminary data from Europe’s Copernicus Climate Change Service show the global average temperature on Nov. 20, 2026, was 2.12°C above the preindustrial average, a record daily anomaly attributed to human-driven warming and a strengthening El Niño. Climate Central scientist Zachary Labe said days at least 2°C above pr
science.content: Preliminary data from Europe’s Copernicus Climate Change Service show the global average temperature on Nov. 20, 2026, was 2.12°C above the preindustrial average, a record daily anomaly attributed to human-driven warming and a strengthening El Niño. Climate Central scientist Zachary Labe said days at least 2°C above preindustrial levels could recur over the next few months as El Niño develops. Separate research led by the University of Melbourne found that atmospheric moisture moving toward Antarctica often preceded daily global temperature peaks during Southern Hemisphere winter. The 2026 Antarctic ozone hole ranked seventh largest in 48 years of observations; scientists attributed its expansion mainly to an unusually strong polar vortex and said ozone-depleting chemicals would have made it larger.
science.image_alt: Earth sets record heat anomaly as Antarctic ozone hole ranks seventh largest

science.title: November Beaver Moon begins series of close full moons through February
science.summary: November’s full Beaver Moon peaks at 9:53 a.m. Eastern time on Tuesday, Nov. 24, when it will be below the horizon in North America. Observers there can look for it rising around sunset. The moon will be about 224,170 miles from Earth, close enough to qualify as a supermoon under some definitions, and should appear onl
science.content: November’s full Beaver Moon peaks at 9:53 a.m. Eastern time on Tuesday, Nov. 24, when it will be below the horizon in North America. Observers there can look for it rising around sunset. The moon will be about 224,170 miles from Earth, close enough to qualify as a supermoon under some definitions, and should appear only slightly larger and brighter than an average full moon. The next full moon falls on Dec. 24 and is expected to be the closest in the sequence, at about 221,667 miles. Further full moons are due Jan. 22 and Feb. 20. Sources describe the sequence as either three or four consecutive supermoons. Near moonrise, the moon may look especially large because of the horizon-related “moon illusion,” not because it is closer at that moment.
science.image_alt: November Beaver Moon begins series of close full moons through February

science.title: Army schedules 68-barrel Iowa blast despite court-ordered pause
science.summary: The U.S. Army plans to detonate 68 barrels of degraded lead azide on Wednesday, Nov. 25, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown, despite a federal appeals court order pausing the explosives disposal permit. The Army says it will rely on a separate emergency exception to proceed, arguing that the material cou
science.content: The U.S. Army plans to detonate 68 barrels of degraded lead azide on Wednesday, Nov. 25, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown, despite a federal appeals court order pausing the explosives disposal permit. The Army says it will rely on a separate emergency exception to proceed, arguing that the material could explode without warning as temperatures fall. The Iowa Environmental Council, Sierra Club and Earthjustice challenged the plan over the risk that a blast could spread lead-bearing dust. The Justice Department says a controlled detonation is safer than an uncontrolled explosion. The groups say invoking emergency powers would bypass the court’s review and have asked to submit additional evidence challenging the Army’s risk assessment. The Army moved the operation from Monday to Wednesday, saying the later date allows for favorable weather and time to put mitigation measures in place. The groups’ legal challenge remains active, while the Army says it intends to proceed under the emergency exception.
science.image_alt: Army schedules 68-barrel Iowa blast despite court-ordered pause

science.title: Deep-sea robot finds deepest volcanic deposits near Challenger Deep
science.summary: The remotely operated vehicle Jason/Medea has found what researchers describe as the deepest documented underwater pyroclastic deposits, on the Mariana Trench wall about 6,000 meters below sea level. The rocks provide evidence of volcanic flows in the trench’s western forearc, where geologists expected little volcanic
science.content: The remotely operated vehicle Jason/Medea has found what researchers describe as the deepest documented underwater pyroclastic deposits, on the Mariana Trench wall about 6,000 meters below sea level. The rocks provide evidence of volcanic flows in the trench’s western forearc, where geologists expected little volcanic activity because the mantle is generally not hot enough to melt. The findings were published Nov. 23 in Frontiers in Earth Science. The team’s observations support the idea that the Pacific Plate bends steeply as it sinks beneath the Mariana plate. That could help explain Challenger Deep’s depth and bring magma-generating processes closer to the trench. But researchers have not identified the eruption sites or established how eruptions could produce these deposits under immense water pressure. They say further sampling and radiometric dating are needed. Jason/Medea cannot reach the seafloor below 6,500 meters, while Challenger Deep extends to about 11,000 meters.
science.image_alt: Deep-sea robot finds deepest volcanic deposits near Challenger Deep

science.title: ESA reports software-related thruster glitch during BepiColombo
science.summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) said a software issue shortened one of BepiColombo’s thruster burns during its Mercury orbit insertion. The joint European-Japanese spacecraft entered orbit successfully on Nov. 21 and remains safe. Mission teams at the European Space Operations Centre are investigating the cause, and ES
science.content: The European Space Agency (ESA) said a software issue shortened one of BepiColombo’s thruster burns during its Mercury orbit insertion. The joint European-Japanese spacecraft entered orbit successfully on Nov. 21 and remains safe. Mission teams at the European Space Operations Centre are investigating the cause, and ESA said it would provide an update on Monday, Nov. 23. BepiColombo carries two orbiters that have traveled together for eight years: ESA’s Mercury Planetary Orbiter and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, called Mio. They are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10, with routine science operations planned to begin in April 2027. The mission will investigate Mercury’s interior, magnetic field and surface, including the origins of its polar ice and unusual surface hollows. ESA said teams were investigating the issue and would provide further information on Monday.
science.image_alt: ESA reports software-related thruster glitch during BepiColombo

sports.title: McBurnie’s stoppage-time double gives Hull win over second-placed Brighton
sports.summary: Hull City beat second-placed Brighton 2-0 at the MKM Stadium on Sunday, with Oli McBurnie scoring twice in stoppage time to end Hull’s eight-match Premier League winless run. Brighton defender João Costinha was sent off for a second yellow card in the 89th minute; McBurnie put Hull ahead in the 92nd and added a second
sports.content: Hull City beat second-placed Brighton 2-0 at the MKM Stadium on Sunday, with Oli McBurnie scoring twice in stoppage time to end Hull’s eight-match Premier League winless run. Brighton defender João Costinha was sent off for a second yellow card in the 89th minute; McBurnie put Hull ahead in the 92nd and added a second in the 95th. Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis kept Brighton out with a series of saves, including several close-range stops, while Regan Slater cleared a chip from Charalampos Kostoulas off the line. The win lifted newly promoted Hull to 11th on 14 points; Brighton stayed second on 22, six behind leaders Arsenal, after missing the chance to narrow the gap. Hull’s next league match is away to Crystal Palace, while Brighton are scheduled to host Newcastle United.
sports.image_alt: McBurnie’s stoppage-time double gives Hull win over second-placed Brighton

sports.title: Gerwyn Price ends four-year major drought with fourth Grand Slam title
sports.summary: Welsh darts player Gerwyn Price beat Dutchman Gian van Veen 16-11 in Wolverhampton on Sunday to win his fourth Grand Slam of Darts title, ending a four-year wait for a major title. The 41-year-old had lost three major finals this year; the victory was his first PDC ranking and televised major win since 2022. The final
sports.content: Welsh darts player Gerwyn Price beat Dutchman Gian van Veen 16-11 in Wolverhampton on Sunday to win his fourth Grand Slam of Darts title, ending a four-year wait for a major title. The 41-year-old had lost three major finals this year; the victory was his first PDC ranking and televised major win since 2022. The final was level at 7-7 before Price won six consecutive legs. Van Veen won two legs after the break, but Price held on to win the match and collect £200,000. Van Veen said he had missed chances and called the final score flattering, while praising Price for taking his opportunities. The win lifted Price to world No. 3. He and Van Veen are due to compete in the Players Championship Finals, which begin Friday. The event will affect Price’s position in the order of merit and his seeding for the World Championship, which starts December 11.

sports.content: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf was ejected in the third quarter of a 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Nov. 22 after two personal foul penalties, including one for an altercation in which he appeared to poke Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean near the eye. Metcalf left with one catch for two yards, and the NFL will review the incident for possible additional discipline, including a suspension that could keep him out of Pittsburgh’s Friday game against Denver. Metcalf, 28, entered Sunday with 35 catches, 432 yards and two touchdowns. He served a two-game suspension in 2025 after an altercation with a Detroit Lions fan. Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said the team would address the incident, while DeJean said he did not take it personally. Pittsburgh fell to 6-4 with its second straight loss, leaving it one and a half games behind Cincinnati in the AFC North. The Steelers await the NFL’s ruling as they prepare to host the Broncos on Friday.

sports.content: The Chicago Bears beat the New Orleans Saints 21-13 on Sunday at Soldier Field for their fifth consecutive win, improving to 8-2. Chicago’s defense recorded six sacks and forced turnovers, while quarterback Caleb Williams threw two touchdown passes. Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons had three sacks in his third game since joining the Bears. The Bears next face the Lions in Detroit on Thanksgiving Day, with both teams at 8-2 and competing for the NFC North lead. Chicago scored no touchdowns in the second half, and Williams finished 15 of 23 for 181 yards. Bears head coach Ben Johnson said the run game fell short of the team’s efficiency target. The Bears and Lions are also scheduled to meet on Jan. 3.

sports.content: Marc Márquez secured his eighth MotoGP premier-class world title on Sunday by finishing eighth at the Portuguese Grand Prix in Portimão, clinching the championship with one round remaining. The Ducati rider now shares the class record with Giacomo Agostini and has 10 world titles across all motorcycle categories. The 33-year-old overcame injuries and a 102-point deficit to Aprilia rider Marco Bezzecchi after seven rounds. Márquez had surgery after a crash at the French Grand Prix and missed races before making up the deficit despite Aprilia’s strong season. A final-lap crash by Diogo Moreira lifted Márquez from ninth to eighth in Portugal, securing the title. Márquez nearly clinched the title in Saturday’s sprint but crashed while running third. Bezzecchi won Sunday’s race ahead of Aprilia teammate Jorge Martín and Trackhouse rider Raúl Fernández. The season ends at Valencia next weekend, with Martín and Bezzecchi separated by two points in the standings.

sports.content: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes says no talks are underway over a new contract. The club has made an offer, but he has put discussions aside while the team tries to recover from a poor start. His current deal expires at the end of this season, but United have an option to extend it by 12 months, through June 2028. Fernandes rejected claims that he wants higher wages or a longer deal, saying he has chosen to stay despite opportunities elsewhere and would leave if the club decided it was time to part ways. United were 19th in the Premier League, with one win from their first 10 league matches, before new head coach Mauricio Pochettino’s first game against Liverpool on Sunday. Fernandes said winning games must take priority over contract talks.

sports.content: The New York Mets have agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with left-hander Tarik Skubal, the largest deal ever for a full-time Major League Baseball pitcher, subject to a physical. Its $50 million average annual value also sets a pitching record. The 30-year-old joins a Mets team that finished last in the National League East at 74-88 in 2026, with its starters’ 4.47 ERA ranking 23rd in the majors. Skubal won American League Cy Young Awards in 2024 and 2025 and posted a 2.72 ERA with 186 strikeouts in 158⅔ innings in 2026 for Detroit and the Los Angeles Dodgers. The Dodgers acquired him from Detroit in August, but he chose New York after meeting with the Mets, the Dodgers, the Toronto Blue Jays and the San Diego Padres. The Mets reached the agreement just over a week before the current collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1, when a lockout is expected if owners and the players’ union do not reach a new deal. The Mets have not announced the signing; it becomes official after Skubal passes his physical.

sports.content: New Zealand batted out 120 overs to draw the first Test against India in Wellington, finishing at 239 for five as Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips resisted the visitors’ final-day push. India had declared at 720 for nine—its highest Test innings total in New Zealand—and led by 352 runs after dismissing the hosts for 368. New Zealand began the final day at 119 for two. India took three wickets, including Devon Conway for 65 and Rachin Ravindra for 37, before Mitchell and Phillips put on an unbeaten 63. Mitchell made 49 from 186 balls and Phillips 26 from 126. The captains shook hands with 15 overs remaining on a Basin Reserve pitch that offered little help to the bowlers. The draw gave both teams four World Test Championship points. India’s points percentage fell from 51.52 to 50, leaving it fourth. The second Test begins at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on November 27.
